title: How to set a new header in pyspark dataframe?
question:
I'm loading a csv into a dataframe of type:

Column A Column B
Cell 1 Cell 2
Cell 3 Cell 4

The header row is "nonsense", the actual header is in row 1, but I want to change the header names based on a schema mapping. e.g changing "FirstName" to "first_name".

I can manage to drop the 1st row if I load the csv with "header=False" (raw2 = spark.createDataFrame(raw.tail(raw.count()-1), raw.schema)), but not sure how to efficiently set the header and then change the values according to the mapping I have.

There is about 60 columns and 600 rows.

This is how I'm loading it:

raw = (spark.read
    .options(
        header=False,                 # use file headers; we'll map by name
        sep=",",
        multiLine=True,              # allow embedded newlines in quotes
        encoding="cp1252",           # handles those smart quotes/Â artifacts
        quote='"',
        escape='"',
        mode="PERMISSIVE",
        columnNameOfCorruptRecord="_corrupt"
    )
    .csv(path)
answer:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("RenameColumns").getOrCreate()

data = [("Alice", 25, "New York"), ("Bob", 30, "San Francisco")]
columns = ["name", "age", "city"]
df = spark.createDataFrame(data, columns)

rename_map = {"name": "user_name", "age": "user_age", "city": "user_city"}

for old_name, new_name in rename_map.items():
    df = df.withColumnRenamed(old_name, new_name)

df.show()
